blocks.text: The wish, and the four things it asks for

content.value: Wave 43 died mid-flight on a weekly account limit, not on a defect. It completed 36 of 41 agents, produced ten charter decisions (PDS-D633-D642), and pushed NOTHING. The lead recovered four branches out of their worktrees by hand and opened #9332, #9333, #9334, #9335 at 12:15 today. Wave 43's reviewer never ran; its debrief was never written. Those four PRs are UNREVIEWED BY ANYONE, and their commit messages are an author's own account of their own work.

The wish asks for four things: (1) re-derive #9332's live write bypass from source before trusting a word of it; (2) verify the other three the same way; (3) confirm PDS-D633's measurement law - the in-BEAM meter is blind to port children and errs in the one direction a price column must not - and ship its blind-spot sentence in the meter's own moduledoc AND printed output; (4) finish the price column: N of 19 instruments under a required gate, every remaining refusal carrying a measured price, a named environment, or NOT-YET-BUILT.

blocks.text: REFUTATION - the first one, and it is in the wish's own item 4

content.value: The wish states the price column's reason vocabulary is 'exactly three reasons: PRICE, ENVIRONMENT, NOT-YET-BUILT' and that 'the fence' is not an available answer. Wave 43's own PDS-D637 - which the wish is paraphrasing - found by RUN that three is not enough. It names FIVE classes: PRICE, ENVIRONMENT, NOT-YET-BUILT, plus CONTENT-RED (pds-charter-ledger-sweep.sh --selftest is rc=1 on main today at 2.36s user, refusing because an UNRESOLVED-CLAIM ARRIVAL is unadjudicated - neither a price nor an environment) and RED-BY-DESIGN / REPORTER (pds-record-parity.sh's live axis B exits 1 on 59 leaf rows, 48 of them belonging to twelve OTHER epics that never consented to the instrument; the arm is a reporter and must never carry a required check name). A related sixth, HUMAN-GATE, governs the sheet-grid harness, whose own workflow header says it only gates once a human registers it as a required check.

The wish also says pds-record-parity.sh --selftest exits rc=3 with 'unknown argument' and calls that an ENVIRONMENT blocker. Wave 43 did not accept that framing - it walked a DIFFERENT door. #9333 gates scripts/pds-record-parity.test.sh, the instrument's own hermetic two-sided mutation harness (76 checks, zero of which read a live ledger row), at 1.30-1.47s user - the cheapest door in the inventory. So record-parity is not an ENVIRONMENT refusal; its HARNESS is a THROUGH and its LIVE arm is RED-BY-DESIGN. The wish's item 4 is the tenth consecutive dispatch this epic has refuted from the artifact, and it is refuted in the direction of GOOD NEWS.

blocks.text: Direction - three movements, and the third is what makes this a wave and not a cleanup

content.value: The finished experience: at the end of wave 44 a cold reader runs ONE command and gets the epic's honesty column back COMPUTED rather than quoted - every scripts/pds-* instrument, its gate status derived from the two things that actually make a door (a test file that shells it, and a matching ELIXIR_TEST_ONLY_PATHS line), its refusal class, and its price in the unit PDS-D633 says is legal. A new pds-* script arrives as an UNDISPOSED row and the thing goes red. A door that quietly stops running goes red. And the number that appears in the charter next wave is a number nobody typed.

blocks.text: Movement 1 - LAND THE RECOVERED WORK, WITH INDEPENDENCE THAT IS REAL

content.value: Charter #9312 merges FIRST and alone, because until it does every D633+ citation a builder would carry points at nothing on origin/main. Then the four slice PRs, each with an independent re-derivation that does NOT read the branch's own test as its oracle. #9332 gets the full treatment: the source-level order defect is already confirmed (cond arm 1 = caps.write, arm 2 = restricted?, and restricted? already contains share_access == :read), so the open question is REACHABILITY - can a real signed-in NON-MEMBER, through a real non-admin route, hold share_access: :read and caps.write == true simultaneously? That is the whole claim, and it must be re-derived through LiveScope.assign_scope -> authorize_read/4, not asserted from a fixture the branch authored.

One suspected defect the wave carries in already, found while reading the diff and NOT yet proven: #9332's membership collapse routes through loadable_principal?/1, which accepts only %ApiToken{} and %User{}. Tenancy.Auth.authorize/3 on origin/main has a THIRD clause at :200 for %Barkpark.Content.CallerContext{}. If a socket's principals list can ever carry a CallerContext, the collapse silently drops a principal that authorize/3 would have decided - a behaviour change dressed as a round-trip saving, in the same slice as a security fix. Survey question 3 exists to settle it before a builder inherits it.

blocks.text: Movement 3 - THE DOOR CENSUS: the price column stops being prose

content.value: This is the bold one. PDS-D637's column is, today, forty lines of charter prose sitting on an unmerged PR - and PDS-D633's own closing sentence is that a number from a meter must live in the instrument's moduledoc and printed output, NEVER in prose a copy-paste can drop. The column violates the law that produced it. Wave 44 turns it into an instrument: enumerate scripts/pds-*.{sh,exs} for the denominator; for each row DERIVE the gate status from two independent legs - leg A, a '../../../scripts/...' string literal in an api/test/** file that actually shells it; leg B, that same path present in elixir-path-escape-check.sh's declared set - and report THROUGH only when BOTH hold. One leg without the other is exactly the wave-42 #9290/#9292 defect (Test skipped while Elixir gate passed in 3s on the skip shim), and this makes that defect impossible to reintroduce quietly rather than merely remembered.

Every non-THROUGH row carries a class from D637's FIVE (not three) and, for PRICE rows, a figure with the meter named. An instrument with no disposition is UNDISPOSED and the census exits non-zero - the same fail-closed shape the receipt census already uses. It prints D633's blind-spot sentence in its own output. And it rides its own door: it is an instrument, so it gets a test file and a path-set line like every other, which is the self-referential proof that the derivation works.

blocks.text: Direction debate - the rivals, and why this one won
Rival A - RECOVERY ONLY

content.value: Spend the whole wave making wave 43's four branches independently bulletproof and merged, plus the charter, and ship nothing new. The case for it is strong and honest: an unreviewed authorization change is the single riskiest object in the repo right now, and a wave that merges it carelessly while chasing new capability has failed at the only thing that mattered. It was rejected because it under-uses the wave, not because it is wrong: four PRs of independent re-derivation is roughly one round, and the fold plus the ladder are DESIGNED work with their obligations already derived by run - leaving them unbuilt for a second consecutive wave is how wave 43's best output rots. Rival A's real contribution survives: movement 1 goes first, alone, and no slice PR merges on its own author's oracle.

blocks.text: Rival B - ADVANCE ONLY

content.value: Treat the four branches as inherited fact, merge them on their green, and spend the wave taking the door from 3 of 19 to 6 or 7. Rejected outright: it is precisely the move the wish forbids, and the epic's own law forbids it too. A commit message is an exit code with better prose. Merging #9332 on its own test's word is 'a gate lies when its green costs nothing to produce', committed by the wave that coined the sentence.

blocks.text: Rival C - THE DOOR CENSUS (winner, as movement 3 of three)

content.value: The winning insight is that the epic has spent four waves arguing about a column it has never computed. Every wave restates the roster, re-prices some rows, and writes the total into the charter by hand - and PDS-D636 records that the census itself carries a FALSE SENTENCE about its own gating on main today. That is the exact failure mode this epic exists to end, committed by the epic, about the epic. Making the column an instrument is the epic's own law turned inward one more notch, and it is cheap: the derivation is two greps over files that already exist, and the prior art is already on main (api/test/barkpark/pds_residue_lens_test.exs).

blocks.text: The sharpest attack on the winner, and how the wave absorbs it

content.value: THE ATTACK: the door census is a THIRD census. This epic already has a receipt census, a residue lens, a ledger census, a record-parity arm and a charter-ledger sweep - nineteen instruments, three of which run anywhere. Building a twentieth instrument to count the nineteen is the purest possible instance of an epic measuring itself instead of shipping. And it will be WRONG on day one: leg A ('a test file shells it') has at least three encodings in the repo already (System.cmd with a module attribute, Code.require_file, a bare relative path), so a naive derivation will under-count and print a number LOWER than the truth - a different lie, in a friendlier direction.

HOW THE WAVE ABSORBS IT. First, the door census is movement THREE of three - it ships only if movements 1 and 2 are honest, and the wave is graded on the security fix and the merges regardless. Second, the under-count objection becomes the instrument's design: the census is FAIL-CLOSED on ambiguity - a pds-* script it cannot dispose is UNDISPOSED and reds, and a test-side reference it cannot classify is an ERROR, never a silent 'not gated'. That makes the day-one wrongness LOUD instead of quiet, and the surveyors are tasked (question 4) with enumerating every encoding of leg A that exists on main before a builder writes a regex. Third, if the survey shows the derivation cannot be made honest cheaply, the fallback is smaller and still real: a self-check that the two legs AGREE for every already-gated instrument - which alone would have caught #9290 and #9292.

BUT THE BYPASS IS NARROWER THAN THE SOCKET GATE, and this decides how it must be verified. For PLAIN socket events the :live_scope_readonly hook halts the event anyway, so a verifier reproducing through a plain event sees green FOR THE WRONG REASON. blocks.text: Decisions - PDS-D643 through D652, each with its one-line why

content.value: These mirror the charter (PR #9353); the charter is the epic's memory, this Paper is the wave's story. Because that PR may not be on main while the builders fly, the decisions are here in full.

items.value: D643 - Movement 1 landed WHILE wave 44 verified it, charter last. Why: 13 dangling citations shipped, and #9334's green was a zero-second skip shim with ZERO gate legs - this epic's own law broken on this epic's own PR.

D644 - #9332 is sound, its suspected own defect is void, and the bypass is NOT closed for the pure grant grade. Why: the narrowing hook is :handle_event and the component route is handle_info, so Access.validate/3 is never consulted. Denying readonly_posture? would be the WRONG fix - the narrowing must travel into the door.

D645 - The fold is recoverable, not rebuildable, and git-grep cannot see stranded work. Why: uncommitted work is the only kind that CAN be stranded, so any git-based sweep systematically misses exactly what it is looking for.

D646 - 210 s is leaf CPU, not a gate budget. Why: a required gate enforces WALL, the driver is serial and prints nothing until the last case returns, and an in-flight run is indistinguishable from a hang by stdout alone.
D647 - The ledger-census door is re-priced and 'viable' is dead. Why: 42.6-49.3 s CPU and 144 checks, and the count is load-independent so this is staleness, not mismeasurement.

D648 - Wall is not a measurable property of a door; the unit is CPU = user + sys, labelled LOCAL. Why: a FIXED workload swung 5.8x at constant load while its user CPU held to 27%, and on the hetzner door sys EXCEEDS user, understating it 2.1x as a pure CPU fact.

D649 - The agreement check cannot fail; leg A must be attribute-bound AND executed. Why: leg A implies leg B by an existing required ratchet, and a comment-blind extractor lets one comment line plus the declaration the ratchet forces manufacture a THROUGH.

D650 - The denominator is 19 and the inventory's owner is the INSTRUMENT'S OWN PRINTED OUTPUT. Why: no doc owns the fact-topic, the repo caps cards at 7, and an appendix would push success-claim-census.md past its budget.

D651 - The palette red is a harness attribution bug, not a contrast defect. Why: a generated :root block was inserted ABOVE the dark block, so an ordinal read compares dark hues against WHITE - and the standing task about it would send a builder to change a hue that passes at 7.27:1.

D652 - What wave 44 cut, with reasons: the ledger-census door (price), the charter sweep (45 hand rulings, gated on this charter merging, and its second read FAILS OPEN), and the sheet-grid reader half (D641, deliberate).

PDS-D654 - A GATE THAT DOES NOT TRIGGER ON ITS OWN SUBJECT IS GREEN FOR FREE. sheet-grid-js.yml runs a harness that parses root.html.heex, presence_state.ex and tokens_gen.ex, and triggered on NONE of them - so the contrast gate never ran on a PR that changed a hue, a background token, or the presence palette. D633's law in its cheapest form yet: no skip shim, no vacuous assertion, just a paths: list that omits the subject. Repaired in #9379.

PDS-D655 - TWO INSTRUMENTS SHIPPED CONTRADICTORY PROSE ABOUT THE SAME FINDING, IN THE SAME WAVE. pds-door-census.sh printed the meter blindness as a 236x real/user RATIO; pds-elixir-receipt-census.exs refuted exactly that on its own runs (113x, then 123x, for the SAME fan-out, because real counts WAITING). Reconciled in review onto the load-independent leaf-metered FLOOR. The rule: when a finding ships inside more than one instrument, ONE owns the sentence and the others cite it - the same argument the census's own @blind_spot attribute makes, one level up.

A FLAKE, FILED RATHER THAN SWALLOWED. The first full studio-suite run scored 1 failure in ChatRenderGoldenTest's sidebar byte-lock (golden 6554 bytes, region 6554 bytes, first diff at 723 - a same-length CONTENT SWAP). It passes in isolation and passed on re-run of the identical tree. Filed as task-441f5a5669e0ab6b. A golden that reds only sometimes trains reviewers to re-run until green, which is this epic's own defect class.

THE HOST WAS NOT QUIET, AND THAT PROVED D605 BY ACCIDENT. The reviewer's census read user cpu 17330 ms against wall clock 95801 ms on a box carrying 24 stray busy-loop processes four days old. The wall figure is the LOAD; the CPU figure is the CODE.

blocks.text: Ledger audit

items.value: All four slice tasks are lifecycle in_progress with merge-gated criteria left OPEN for the lead - correct, none closed early.

Evidence was stamped AS THE BUILDERS WORKED, not batched: each carries per-criterion evidence quoting run output, and two carry honest --miss records rather than fabricated flips (pds-w44-census-fold-and-blindspot criterion 8, the lv_verdict/5 cond reorder; pds-w44-palette-harness-repair criterion 7, the PR body a builder cannot write because builders do not push).

Each of the other three tasks gained a review_status naming its final branch, its PR, and which gate legs the REVIEWER re-ran (as distinct from which the builder claimed).
No task outside this wave was mutated. One NEW task was filed and published: task-441f5a5669e0ab6b (the golden byte-lock flake), parented to the epic.

blocks.text: Grade - A-

content.value: EARNED, not awarded. What is genuinely strong: three of four slices closed a defect that was REAL and proved it by substitution rather than by reading, and every one of them refuted part of its own brief from the artifact - the palette slice found a THIRD stale coupling nobody had priced (--fg-muted was matched for an hsl() both themes author as var(--muted-text), so that check had found zero declarations and could never have run), and the census slice refused the ratio its dispatch demanded. The security slice is the wave's best work: it declined the obvious fix (widening Caps.write_capable?/2, which is shared with the SheetGrid prop and has no target), declined the obvious predicate (Access.admits_desk?/3, whose type/doc_id overwrite IS the bug), and carries a positive control proving a legitimate grantee still writes.

What falls short. (1) A whole slice died between its last stamp and its first commit and NOTHING in the wave's own reporting said so - it took a branch-vs-ledger diff to find a finished instrument one cycle away from deletion. That is the sixth consecutive wave to strand built work, and it is the single reason this is not an A. (2) Two instruments shipped contradictory prose about the same finding in the same wave - a coherence failure the wave had every opportunity to catch, since one slice explicitly refuted the other's figure in its own commit message. (3) The security slice's shipped non-vacuity test is a local constant-false STUB, not the reverted arm; the real revert was run and recorded in the stamp, but the artifact that MERGES cannot reproduce it - the reviewer had to re-run the mutation by hand to confirm. (4) Coverage is honestly partial and says so: paper_ops/2 and document_op/2 carry the new arm but are proven by READING, and the census's ExUnit rider was never run locally.

No bloat: 489 lines for the security slice including a 361-line test, 333 for the census fold, 86 for the palette repair. Nothing was redesigned; the reviewer's edits are two latent-hazard closures and one prose reconciliation. Tree-tidiness was not pursued and has no value here.

blocks.text: What the next wave should take

content.value: MERGE ROUND 1 FIRST, IN THIS ORDER: #9377 (the security fix - it is the only thing in this wave that closes a live escalation), then #9379 (it turns the red Sheet-grid hook unit harness green, which is currently the only non-advisory red on the still-open #9335), then #9378 and #9380. Two of the four are owed a genuinely independent second reviewer before merge, and this workflow spawns exactly one reviewer, so that dispatch is a MANUAL LEAD STEP: #9377 (security / tenancy) and #9380 (whether leg A admits a fraudulent THROUGH - and it never got its builder's own review dispatch, so it has had ONE pair of eyes on 37 KB of shell).

THEN THE DEFERRED ROUND-2 SLICES, EACH AS ITS DEPENDENCY MERGES: pds-w44-judgment-coverage-ladder after #9378 (both rewrite the census and every line number shifts - re-derive anchors at the new base, and PROVEN-BACKED must be one Enum.count over one MapSet.union, never an addition); pds-w44-hetzner-offline-door after #9380 (it edits the same declared set, so dispatching beside it produces a conflict, not a build - and BOTH legs or neither: the instrument AND its ELIXIR_TEST_ONLY_PATHS entry); pds-w44-charter-sweep-adjudication after the charter PR #9353 merges (the candidate vocabulary is MINED FROM THE CHARTER, so adjudicating before it lands produces a fresh red the moment it does - and this wave's own wave-log entry moved that vocabulary again).

AND ONE NEW STANDING CHORE, from D653: every review must diff each wave task's stated branch against origin/main before it grades anything. An empty diff on a stamped task is a stranded slice, and the built-slice handoff structurally cannot report one.
